name: Suiko
author: Adrien Asselineau

sections.description:
Suiko (https://getsuiko.com) is a content platform for teams that manage SEO and GEO content: it prepares the brief from what Google shows and from your knowledge base, guides your writers with a content score, checks every fact against your sources, publishes to your site, and keeps your published articles true over time by proposing updates when a price, a rule, a date or a lead time changes. This plugin connects your WordPress site to Suiko. Once connected:

  • New articles written in Suiko arrive in WordPress in one click, as drafts or published, with their title tag, meta description and focus keyword written into Yoast SEO or Rank Math (both tested; without an SEO plugin, the post title and excerpt are used).
  • Updates with verified facts: Suiko reads your published posts and pages, spots what is out of date, and the update you approve on Suiko arrives in WordPress as a draft linked to the live article, with a one-click “Apply this Suiko update” action. Or, if you prefer, it replaces the live article directly; the previous version stays in the article’s revisions.
  • Performance stays on Suiko’s side: clicks, impressions and position of each page from Google Search Console, and whether the page is cited in Google’s AI Overviews. The plugin itself sends nothing to Google.
  • Nothing else: the key only lets Suiko read published posts and pages, and create or update posts and pages. Requests run with no logged-in user, so they never have an administrator’s rights, and WordPress filters their HTML like any untrusted content. No user accounts, no plugins, no themes, no settings are read or changed. Page builders (Elementor, Divi, WPBakery, Beaver Builder, Bricks) are read but not written: you apply those updates by hand.

Connecting takes one click: Settings > Suiko > “Connect to Suiko”. You confirm on Suiko and come straight back. Nothing to copy.

External services

This plugin connects your site to the Suiko service (https://getsuiko.com), operated by Adrien Asselineau, Lisbon. It talks to two addresses:

  • app.getsuiko.com, when you click “Connect to Suiko”: your browser is sent there with a one-time pairing code, your site address and name; Suiko then calls your site once to exchange that code for a key. Afterwards, Suiko reads your published articles and files updates through your site’s REST API (/wp-json/suiko/v1), authenticated with that key. Nothing is sent unless you connected the site, and disconnecting stops it.
  • getsuiko.com/wordpress/suiko.json, twice a day at most, to learn whether a newer version of the plugin exists (self-hosted builds only; the WordPress.org build does not do this). Only the plugin version and your WordPress version are sent.

Terms: https://getsuiko.com/terms/ · Privacy: https://getsuiko.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Settings > Suiko and click “Connect to Suiko”.
  3. Confirm on Suiko. You are back in WordPress: connected.
sections.faq:
Does it work with Yoast SEO or Rank Math?

Yes, both are tested: the SEO title, meta description and focus keyword are read and written back on update. Page builders (Elementor, Divi, WPBakery, Beaver Builder, Bricks) are read but not written: you apply those updates by hand.

Does Suiko publish on my site without asking?

Not by default. Updates arrive as drafts; you apply them in one click. You can switch to direct replacement in Settings > Suiko.

What does the plugin store?

A hash of the key Suiko uses to talk to your site (never the key itself), the publication mode, the name of your Suiko organisation and which user connected the site (new articles are credited to them). Disconnecting removes them.
sections.changelog:
0.1.2

  • Settings page: the new Suiko logo and colours. Nothing else changes.

0.1.1

  • Requests from Suiko no longer act as a WordPress user: new articles are credited to the user who connected the site, and content goes through the standard WordPress HTML filter.

0.1.0

  • First version: one-click pairing, article reading, updates as drafts or direct, Yoast SEO and Rank Math fields.
